newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes flounder in high profile sell-off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes flounder in high profile sell-off.

text.p: Dramatic selling in the NYMEX futures market staggered outright prices for U.S. crudes, while supply concerns deflated domestic grade differentials.
Cash traders said the futures market set the tone for trading, with technically-inspired selling allowing July futures to settle down 87 cents at $18.82 a barrel.

July benchmark cash West Texas Intermediate/Cushing maintained a 18-20 cents premium to the futures screen on Exchange for Physical strength. Final markings for the turbulent week put cash July WTI/Cushing at $18.95-19.05 a barrel, some 80 cents weaker than late session Thursday.
At the same time futures and cash outrights lost ground, the domestic grade markets retreated on fundamental pressures.

West Texas Sour/Midland and Eugene Island sours made the most obvious moves, shedding 10-20 cents from Thursday. Eugene Island sold at WTI/Cushing -$1.90, while WTS/Midland ranged around a $1.75 discount most of the day.
"There was perhaps more confidence of Venezuelan crude availability in the Gulf," said one sour crude dealer.

Besides Latin American crude, the sour market was hit by weak prices in Asia and the decision midweek to renew the Iraqi oil-for-food accord from June 8 to December 4, keeping 600,000 to 700,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi exports in the mix.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James ended at a 25-20 cents discount, selling as weak as 27 cents under WTI, declining from 17-15 cents discounts on Thursday. LLS started the week bid and offered at minus 16-12 cents.

Sweet barrels were pressured by a weak Dated Brent market and a large number of West African barrels on offer. A European trade house was heard to be the most active seller in the LLS market, possibly in moves related to North Sea Brent.

Other domestic grade deals were seen for Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at -70 cents, and for Postings Plus at $1.82, 10 cents weaker than Thursday. July/August WTI spreads were at minus 33 cents on the futures screen, but EFP premiums reduced the actual roll to minus 10-12 cents, traders said.
